thread:
sec-bot: automated secret-scan detected a potential GCP service-account JSON key in a public commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/commit/7f3c2a9

maria: FYI found by pre-commit scanner. file: infra/ci/sa-keys/service-account.json (accidentally pushed). commit 7f3c2a9. the key looks valid (client_email present).

sam: ack. tagging irene for rotation, julio for logs/usage. we should assume compromise until proven otherwise.

irene: oncall +1. i'll revoke the key now and rotate. where's the service account name?

maria: name is: redwood-ci-deployer@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com. minimal perms? appears to have storage.admin on a couple buckets (too wide).

julio: i'll query cloud audit logs for any use in the past 24h and check for external IPs. running: 
```
# list last 48h admin activity for this SA
gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail="redwood-ci-deployer@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com"' --freshness=48h --project=redwood-prod --format=json | jq '.[] | {timestamp: .timestamp, method: .protoPayload.methodName, resource: .resource}'
```

sec-bot: note: repository commit made 2026-03-19T14:22:11Z by user `dev-automation`

sam: irene — when you revoke, please also delete the key from the repo and create a forced rotation PR for any workflows referencing the SA. tag me on the PR.

irene: doing revoke now. running: 
```
gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=redwood-ci-deployer@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-prod
# identify key id
gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete KEY_ID --iam-account=redwood-ci-deployer@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-prod
```

maria: i've opened a DL ticket INC-2026-118 and pinged legal & compliance. also notifying internal infra owners to scan other repos for similar files (grep + secret-scan).

julio: preliminary logs: no external egress from that SA in the last 72h, only internal CI job runs from 10.2.0.0/16 (we still need to validate tokens used elsewhere). i'll post exact query results in the ticket once done.

sam: two follow-ups: 1) tighten SA IAM to least-privilege (remove storage.admin), 2) move credentials out of plaintext into KMS/secret manager and update CI to fetch at runtime.

maria: agree. also we should enable key expiry on future SA keys and enforce that via IAM policy/gcp org policy if possible.

irene: revoked and deleted the key from the project. deleted the file from the repo and pushed a forced-commit to remove it (PR #432). created replacement SA key with limited scopes and rotated into vault: 
```
# create new key and put in Secret Manager
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create new-key.json --iam-account=redwood-ci-deployer@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-prod
gcloud secrets create redwood/ci/redwood-ci-deployer --data-file=new-key.json --replication-policy="automatic"
```

sam: perfect. pls also rotate any runtime tokens referencing the old key in Dedicated/backups. run quick grep across infra repos and config: `rg "redwood-ci-deployer" -S` and open PRs for updates.

julio: audit results: no sign of key exfiltration. only calls were internal CI using our corporate IP ranges 10.2.0.0/16. Cloud Storage access timestamps match expected CI times. tagging @maria for customer-impact decision.

maria: thanks. I think customer impact is low — SA only touched internal infra buckets and internal staging artifacts. i'm drafting a short blurb for SOC and for support in case customers ask.

sam: long-term actions — (1) enforce repository blocklist for JSON service-account files, (2) integrate KMS/Secret Manager usage in CI templates, (3) add org policy to prevent creating unconstrained SA keys, (4) enable audit sinks to BigQuery for faster queries.

irene: added tasks to INC-2026-118: revoke (done), rotate (done), repo cleanup (done), scan-other-repos (in progress), postmortem doc (assigned to maria).

maria: assigning postmortem to myself. outline: timeline, root cause (credential checked in by automation), containment steps, detection gap, remediation plan (policy + infra changes), and owner list. target to publish internal postmortem in 72h.

sec-bot: reminder: run `secret-scan --fix` across all repos and add pre-commit hook to infra templates.

julio: also recommend enabling CMEK for any customer-sensitive buckets and ensure KMS keys are rotated regularly.

sam: for RBAC: review existing SA roles and create scoped roles for CI; remove the ability for automation to create long-lived user-managed keys. use short-lived tokens where possible.

maria: final ask — please each add a 1-line status to INC-2026-118 when your checks are done. i'll close the incident once postmortem is published and validations complete. thanks all :thumbsup:

irene: closing loop here — all immediate actions done, monitoring for anomalous activity for 7 days. will escalate if anything new shows up.

julio: logging queries, results and commands saved in the incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-118

sam: great work, team.

maria: moving to postmortem doc now.
